rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation is in instance_norm_forward_kernel (non-affine version). ModelNew creates InstanceNorm2dCustom with default affine=True, causing weight and bias to be defined nn.Parameter tensors. In C++, the check 'weight.defined() && bias.defined()' is TRUE, so instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine is always called instead of the mutated instance_norm_forward_kernel.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation affects the non-affine kernel instance_norm_forward_kernel, but the model class ModelNew instantiates InstanceNorm2dCustom with the default affine=True parameter. When affine=True, self.weight and self.bias are initialized as nn.Parameter tensors (ones and zeros respectively). The forward method passes these defined tensors to the CUDA function. In the C++ implementation, the branch condition 'weight.defined() && bias.defined()' evaluates to true when valid tensors are passed, directing execution to instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine. The mutated instance_norm_forward_kernel is therefore never invoked. No input values can alter this execution path since kernel selection depends solely on whether weight/bias tensors are defined, which is determined by model construction.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under current contract. The mutated code is in a kernel that is never called because the model uses affine=True. To kill this mutant would require changing the model construction to use affine=False, which violates the fixed-configuration testing contract.
rounds.recommendations: When creating mutation tests for CUDA kernels with multiple code paths (e.g., affine vs non-affine), ensure the test harness can exercise all paths. Consider parameterizing the model construction or creating separate test fixtures for each kernel variant to achieve complete mutation coverage.
